instruction: Configure Thunderbird to move all incoming messages from 'newsletter@example.com' into the 'Newsletter' folder for the anonym-x2024@outlook.com account, making sure the filter is turned on.

metadata.explanation: This variation asks the user to create a message filter that moves emails from a specific sender to a folder on a specific account. The evaluator uses the existing check_thunderbird_filter function to verify that a filter exists with: (1) enabled='yes', (2) action='Move to folder', (3) actionValue specifying the Newsletter folder with full IMAP URI, and (4) condition checking the 'from' field against 'newsletter@example.com'. The account association is verified by checking the msgFilterRules.dat file in the outlook.office365.com account directory - filters are stored per account, so verifying the correct file path ensures the filter is applied to the anonym-x2024@outlook.com account only.
metadata.verification: The original task uses check_thunderbird_filter to verify email forwarding. This variation uses the same function but checks for a 'Move to folder' action with actionValue pointing to Newsletter folder (imap://anonym-x2024%40outlook.com@outlook.office365.com/Newsletter) and a 'from' sender condition. Account verification is implicit: the result.path points to outlook.office365.com account directory, and Thunderbird stores filters per-account, so verifying this specific file ensures the filter is on the correct account.

llm_judge_reasons: Complete verification coverage: All 5 instruction requirements are correctly verified (100% coverage)
Enabled verification: expected.enabled='yes' correctly verifies filter is enabled
Sender verification: expected.condition=['AND (from,is,newsletter@example.com)'] correctly verifies the sender condition
Folder verification: expected.actionValue='imap://anonym-x2024%40outlook.com@outlook.office365.com/Newsletter' correctly verifies the destination folder is 'Newsletter'

Account verification: Double-verified through (1) result.path points to outlook.office365.com account-specific directory, and (2) actionValue contains account identifier 'anonym-x2024%40outlook.com', ensuring filter is only on the specified account
Action verification: expected.action='Move to folder' correctly verifies the move action

Metric logic correctness: check_thunderbird_filter (thunderbird.py:76-135) parses msgFilterRules.dat, extracts all filter fields (name, enabled, action, actionValue, condition), and uses _match_record to verify expected rules match - logic is sound
Runtime correctness: Metric handles None case (line 90-91), and postconfig appropriately closes Message Filters window before verification
Data flow correctness: get_vm_file retrieves account-specific filter file -> check_thunderbird_filter parses and matches against complete expected rules -> returns 1.0 if all fields match
